Alisha (Marketing): Quick ask — webinar next Tue. We need bench numbers + minimal reproducible payloads for the live demo and press pack. Can eng/runtime do a couple quick sanity runs and hand us: p50/p95/p99 (in ms), tokens generated, model variant names, and a zipped sample of request/response logs?
Mike (eng-runtime): Yup. Which workload exactly — chat (multi-turn) or single-turn generation? streaming or non-streaming? target seq len?
Alisha (Marketing): For the demo: single-turn generative transcript -> ~512 output tokens, streaming enabled. For press pack, also want a non-streamed 128-token run for a short blog stat. Models: latest redwood-v2 and quantized-redwood-v2-8bit.
Raj (eng-runtime): We can run both. Quick clarifying Q: concurrency for the batches? live demo will be 1 connection, but marketing might want a 4-concurrency desktop sim for press numbers.
Alisha (Marketing): Good call — include both: 1x concurrent (demo), 4x concurrent (press sim). Also include batch sizes 1 and 8.
Mike (eng-runtime): Ok working plan: run streaming 512/1x and 4x; non-stream 128/1x and 4x; each on redwood-v2 and redwood-v2-8bit. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and raw logs. Expect to finish tomorrow morning.
Alisha (Marketing): Awesome. Can you also give a tiny curl/SDK snippet we can paste in the slide so the demo team can rehearse? Prefer curl + node SDK.
Mike (eng-runtime): Dropping a minimal curl we use in the runbook:

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-v2","input":"Write a concise product summary.","max_tokens":512,"stream":true}'
```

And a node snippet for non-streaming run: `await client.generate({model:'redwood-v2',input:'TL;DR...',max_tokens:128})`

Raj (eng-runtime): Also adding a small runbook note we'll attach: what to check if numbers look off — CPU pinned, GPU memory OOM, kernel mismatches, and making sure quantized builds use the latest kernel pack.
Sofia (Product): Quick branding/legal check — if we publish p95 numbers in marketing, prefer "typical p95 under X ms for the tested config" and include model/config footnote. Avoid absolute claims.
Mike (eng-runtime): Agreed. We'll produce a small table and an artifacts zip with: `runs/1801234567/metadata.json`, `runs/1801234567/requests.log`, `runs/1801234567/responses.log`, and a one-paragraph methodology note. We'll flag anything flaky.
Alisha (Marketing): Perfect. Can you also include a short 1-sentence blurb we can use in the deck like: "In our tests, redwood-v2 produced 512 tokens with median latency X ms (streaming) on the tested instance." We'll edit numbers once you give final output.
Mike (eng-runtime): Will do. ETA: final artifacts + snippet by 10:30am PT tomorrow. If we hit regressions, we'll call it out.
